cards.front: Recall a key point about Word Order and Conjunctions
cards.back: Whatever comes first in the sentence, the conjugated verb MUST be second. If something other than the subject comes first, the subject swaps places with the verb (verb-subject inversion).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Word Order and Conjunctions
cards.back: When a subordinate clause comes FIRST in the sentence, the main clause that follows has VERB-FIRST-SUBJECT order: "Weil ich krank bin, bleibe ich zu Hause" (NOT "ich bleibe"). The subordinate clause counts as position 1, so the verb of the main clause must be in position 2.

cards.front: What should you know about german exam tips — word order and conjunctions?
cards.back: 1. For Word Order and Conjunctions, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Word Order and Conjunctions, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning
because (e.g. Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin)
that (e.g. Ich denke, dass Deutsch wichtig ist)
when/if (e.g. Wenn ich Zeit habe, gehe ich schwimmen)
although (e.g. Obwohl es regnet, gehen wir aus)
while/during (e.g. Während ich esse, lese ich)
whether/if (e.g. Ich weiß nicht, ob er kommt)
since/because (e.g. Da ich müde bin, gehe ich ins Bett)
word order (e.g. Die Wortstellung ist im Deutschen streng geregelt.)
verb-second rule (e.g. In Hauptsätzen gilt die Verb-Zweit-Regel.)
main clause (e.g. Im Hauptsatz steht das Verb an zweiter Stelle.)
subordinate clause (e.g. Im Nebensatz steht das Verb am Ende.)
